profession.none.1: I still don't know what to do with my life. How did you know what yours was?
profession.none.2: If anyone leaves a workstation free in %2$s, let me know.
profession.none.3: Today I helped everyone a little and nobody thanked me.
profession.none.4: They offered to make me a fisherman, but the water gives me funny looks.
profession.none.5: My mother says at my age she already had three trades. I've got time.
profession.none.6: I tried the anvil and singed my eyebrows. I tried the books and fell asleep.
profession.none.7: Someday someone in %2$s will need me for something. And I'll be ready.
profession.none.8: I've spent all morning watching the others work. It's more tiring than it looks.
profession.none.9: If you know of a trade where nobody gets up at dawn, tell me, %1$s.
profession.none.10: The farmer let me pull weeds. I pulled the carrots too.
profession.none.11: No trade means no orders. It also means no hurry.
profession.none.12: They say the librarian wants an apprentice. I'm just not sure I read well enough.
profession.none.13: When I have a trade, I'll get a hat that says so.

profession.armorer.1: Good armour goes unnoticed until the day you need it.
profession.armorer.2: The bellows of my blast furnace whistle when rain is coming. Never fails.
profession.armorer.3: If you come back with dented armour, bring it to me before it rusts.
profession.armorer.4: Three hauberks half riveted, and the customer has already been round twice.
profession.armorer.5: Put the breastplate on, let me fit it. Deep breath. There. Too tight?
profession.armorer.6: One skeleton's arrow tells me more about a cuirass than any test I could run.
profession.armorer.7: The iron from the mines of %2$s is good, but it puts up a fight in the forge.
profession.armorer.8: Gold helmets shine a lot and stop very little. Tell that to the vain ones.
profession.armorer.9: Every dent you bring me is a story I'd rather not hear in full.
profession.armorer.10: I've smelled of coal so long I don't notice any more. Everyone else does.
profession.armorer.11: I don't sell a shield to someone who can't raise it in time, %1$s.
profession.armorer.12: A loose strap has killed more men than many a sword.
profession.armorer.13: If you find diamonds, think of your chest before your pickaxe.

profession.butcher.1: The smoke from the smoker clings to your clothes for a whole week.
profession.butcher.2: In %2$s nobody goes hungry while I have salt and firewood.
profession.butcher.3: The best chops are winter ones. My grandmother says so, and she is never wrong.
profession.butcher.4: Keep the knife sharp. A blunt one cuts more fingers than meat.
profession.butcher.5: The rabbits round here are scrawny, but a little rosemary sorts them out.
profession.butcher.6: Roast mutton today. Tomorrow, whatever the shepherd brings me.
profession.butcher.7: Nothing of a pig goes to waste: what isn't roasted gets salted.
profession.butcher.8: When %2$s holds a feast, the spit keeps turning all night.
profession.butcher.9: If you hunt anything on the road, %1$s, bring it to me whole. I'll dress it.
profession.butcher.10: A good broth mends a bad day. Two mend a bad winter.
profession.butcher.11: Rotten flesh off a zombie? I wouldn't take it as a gift.
profession.butcher.12: My hands are cracked from all the salt. That's the price of a good ham.
profession.butcher.13: The shepherd and I don't talk much. You can see why.

profession.cartographer.1: Every road I draw ends at another I don't know yet.
profession.cartographer.2: A blank map is the most beautiful thing in the world, %1$s.
profession.cartographer.3: Half the world is left to draw and my hands already shake.
profession.cartographer.4: There's a coastline I can't get to close. Either the map lies or the sea moves.
profession.cartographer.5: Wayfarers bring me names of places. I suspect they make up half of them.
profession.cartographer.6: I need more compasses. The ones I have point true, but they get lost in my drawers.
profession.cartographer.7: At the edge of every map I write "I have not been here". It's the most honest thing I know.
profession.cartographer.8: From the bell tower of %2$s you can see half the valley. The other half I guess.
profession.cartographer.9: If you pass through a swamp, tell me where it ends. Nobody can.
profession.cartographer.10: Ink runs in the damp. That's why I draw the rivers on dry days.
profession.cartographer.11: A good map doesn't tell you where to go, %1$s. It tells you where you are.
profession.cartographer.12: I've drawn roads the brambles swallowed later. Paper remembers what the land forgets.
profession.cartographer.13: People ask me for treasure maps. I make true maps; the treasure is up to you.

profession.cleric.1: The altar candles last longer when the village is at peace.
profession.cleric.2: I have seen things on moonless nights I'd rather not tell.
profession.cleric.3: May the bell of %2$s keep you on the road.
profession.cleric.4: Holy water isn't bought, it's waited for. And the brewing stand is never in a hurry.
profession.cleric.5: They come and tell me things I don't understand. I nod a great deal.
profession.cleric.6: Nether wart smells of brimstone, but it heals what other herbs can't.
profession.cleric.7: When the bell of %2$s rings at the wrong hour, I pray first and ask questions later.
profession.cleric.8: If you're hurt out there, %1$s, don't leave it till tomorrow. Tomorrow it hurts more.
profession.cleric.9: I keep a vial with a ghast tear in it. Don't ask me how I came by it.
profession.cleric.10: Zombies were somebody once. That's why I give thanks every time the sun comes up.
profession.cleric.11: Spider eyes have their uses. None of them pleasant, mind.
profession.cleric.12: The altar has room for all the village's sorrows. Not for all the candles, though.
profession.cleric.13: Some nights the moon won't let me sleep. I know what it brings, and I don't like it.

profession.farmer.1: The wheat is growing tall this year. If it doesn't rain too much, there'll be bread for everyone.
profession.farmer.2: The crows don't dare come near my scarecrow. Well, hardly ever.
profession.farmer.3: The soil of %2$s is grateful if you treat it kindly.
profession.farmer.4: Plant potatoes next to carrots and they quarrel. I've seen it.
profession.farmer.5: The composter stinks, but what comes out of it is worth its weight in gold.
profession.farmer.6: I'm up before the rooster. The rooster just brags about it more.
profession.farmer.7: The pumpkins are huge this year. One of them comes up to my knee.
profession.farmer.8: In %2$s we water with what falls from the sky and what comes up the well.
profession.farmer.9: Rabbits eat my carrots and I eat the rabbits. That's the way of the world.
profession.farmer.10: Tread on my furrows, %1$s, and you'll spend the afternoon picking stones.
profession.farmer.11: Nobody wants beetroot until there's soup.
profession.farmer.12: When the rain comes in its season, there's no sweeter music.
profession.farmer.13: The bees help me with the flowers and I leave their hedge alone. It's a deal.

profession.fisherman.1: The biggest fish is always the one that gets away.
profession.fisherman.2: At dawn the water is so still it looks like glass.
profession.fisherman.3: Once I reeled in a boot full of water. No sign of its owner.
profession.fisherman.4: Cod bite at first light; salmon, whenever they please.
profession.fisherman.5: My rod has more patches than my boat, and my boat has plenty.
profession.fisherman.6: When the float goes under, my heart goes up. Forty years and it's still the same.
profession.fisherman.7: Once I fished an enchanted book out of the river. I sold it before I read it.
profession.fisherman.8: If a pufferfish takes the bait, it goes back in the water. Carefully, and without touching it.
profession.fisherman.9: There are drowned about in the waters of %2$s. I fish well away from the bank.
profession.fisherman.10: Patience is learned on the riverbank, %1$s, not in books.
profession.fisherman.11: If the water bubbles with no wind, that's bad news. I pack up and go.
profession.fisherman.12: I mend the nets at night, by lantern light. Every knot is mine.
profession.fisherman.13: The sea owes you nothing. Whatever it gives, be thankful.

profession.fletcher.1: The best feathers come from old hens. Don't ask me why.
profession.fletcher.2: One straight arrow is worth ten crooked ones.
profession.fletcher.3: If you see flint along the road, save it for me, %1$s.
profession.fletcher.4: Birch for the shaft. For the bow, whatever you like, as long as it doesn't creak.
profession.fletcher.5: The apprentices throw out every wet feather. Then I've nothing to fletch with.
profession.fletcher.6: A flint-tipped arrow doesn't forgive. Mind who you aim it at.
profession.fletcher.7: I've an order of two hundred arrows for the guard of %2$s. I'm on number eighty.
profession.fletcher.8: Cobweb makes the best string. The trouble is going to fetch it.
profession.fletcher.9: Skeletons shoot badly, but they shoot a lot. Keep your head down, %1$s.
profession.fletcher.10: Crossbows are for people with no patience. Pillagers have none.
profession.fletcher.11: I test every arrow on my finger. If it hums crooked, it goes in the fire.
profession.fletcher.12: The hens give me their feathers and I give them my thanks. They get the worse end of it.
profession.fletcher.13: A target with three arrows in the middle is the prettiest thing I've ever seen.

profession.leatherworker.1: Well-tanned leather outlasts a lot of iron.
profession.leatherworker.2: I smell of the cauldron all day, but somebody has to do it.
profession.leatherworker.3: Your boots are crying out for a patch, did you know?
profession.leatherworker.4: Rabbit hide is soft, but it tears if you look at it wrong.
profession.leatherworker.5: I've a saddle half done. The horse is getting restless, and the owner more so.
profession.leatherworker.6: The dye gets under my nails. This month they're purple.
profession.leatherworker.7: You don't notice a good pack until it splits a mile from home.
profession.leatherworker.8: The cows of %2$s give good leather. Trouble is, they give you sad eyes too.
profession.leatherworker.9: If you see hides at the market, %1$s, haggle. They're not worth the asking price.
profession.leatherworker.10: That cauldron has burned me more than a whole summer's sun.
profession.leatherworker.11: I stitch at night, when the village is quiet. The leather tells me where it wants the needle.
profession.leatherworker.12: Leather armour won't stop a sword, but it stops the cold. And the cold kills too.
profession.leatherworker.13: My old gloves have outlived a good many knights.

profession.librarian.1: There is a book on my shelf nobody has ever opened. Not even me.
profession.librarian.2: The history of %2$s fits in three volumes, and one of them is recipes.
profession.librarian.3: Reading at night uses up candles, but saves on boredom.
profession.librarian.4: The smith borrowed a volume on tempering iron two winters ago. I'm still waiting.
profession.librarian.5: Binding books is easy. Getting people not to fold the corners is the hard part.
profession.librarian.6: I have an enchanted book nobody can read. I suspect it's out of pride.
profession.librarian.7: The library of %2$s is small, but every book is where it belongs.
profession.librarian.8: If you're going to touch anything, %1$s, wash your hands. Road dust is merciless.
profession.librarian.9: I keep the village chronicle. So far this year: two weddings and a lost cow.
profession.librarian.10: Squid ink stains worse than any other. That's why it writes better.
profession.librarian.11: Lecterns creak when someone truly reads. Mine hardly ever creak.
profession.librarian.12: They ask me for adventure books, and then they never leave the village.
profession.librarian.13: An empty shelf is a question. A full one is a promise I won't keep.

profession.mason.1: A well-built wall outlasts whoever raises it.
profession.mason.2: The stone of this land is stubborn, like the people of %2$s.
profession.mason.3: If you hear a beam creak, tell me before the mayor.
profession.mason.4: A whole week on the well wall, and the bucket still comes up full of sand.
profession.mason.5: River clay makes good brick. Pond clay is only good for getting filthy.
profession.mason.6: Anyone can put stone on stone. Getting it to stay put is another matter.
profession.mason.7: The mayor wants a new tower in %2$s. I want paying for the last one.
profession.mason.8: A blunt chisel makes you hate granite. A good one makes you love it.
profession.mason.9: If you build anything out there, %1$s, start with the foundations. Everyone knows it; hardly anyone does it.
profession.mason.10: Glazed terracotta is very pretty, but you don't want it on a kitchen floor.
profession.mason.11: My back aches when a frost is coming. The walls feel it too.
profession.mason.12: A wooden house burns. A stone one gets a bit of soot, at worst.
profession.mason.13: Every morning I count the cracks in the wall. Today there's one more.

profession.nitwit.1: Did you know sheep can't swim backwards? I made that up.
profession.nitwit.2: Today I counted the clouds. I got seven. Or six.
profession.nitwit.3: I don't work, but I have opinions on everything. Someone has to.
profession.nitwit.4: I've been thinking about important things. I've forgotten all of them.
profession.nitwit.5: See that cloud? It looked like a chicken. Now it looks like a different chicken.
profession.nitwit.6: They tried to teach me to mend nets. The nets won.
profession.nitwit.7: Everyone in %2$s works so hard. Somebody has to watch how they do it.
profession.nitwit.8: If you're looking for me, %1$s, I'm here. I'm nearly always here.
profession.nitwit.9: Once I chased a rabbit all afternoon. He didn't know where we were going either.
profession.nitwit.10: I like the sound of the bell. I like it less when I'm the one ringing it.
profession.nitwit.11: I fell down the well today. Well, I leaned over it a lot.
profession.nitwit.12: The others have trades; I have ideas. None of them work, but they're mine.
profession.nitwit.13: Why don't creepers have arms? I asked one. Bad idea.

profession.shepherd.1: My sheep know my whistle from across the valley.
profession.shepherd.2: This year's wool is so soft it feels a shame to dye it.
profession.shepherd.3: If you see a stray sheep, it's mine. It's always mine.
profession.shepherd.4: The wolves came last night. The dog heard them before I did, and I before the sheep.
profession.shepherd.5: I shear in spring. Any earlier and the sheep glare at me all month.
profession.shepherd.6: One black sheep in the flock brings luck. Two bring arguments.
profession.shepherd.7: The pastures of %2$s run out early. That's why I take the flock up the hill when it blooms.
profession.shepherd.8: The loom isn't my calling, but someone has to turn the wool into something.
profession.shepherd.9: If you meet a wolf, %1$s, don't run. Well, run if it's after the sheep.
profession.shepherd.10: I dye the wool with whatever I find: poppies, cactus, squid ink. The squid ink smells.
profession.shepherd.11: I count the sheep every night. I'm always one short, and then it turns up on a roof.
profession.shepherd.12: Sheep eat the grass and the grass grows back. If only everything were like that.
profession.shepherd.13: You have to know every sheep by its bleat. I know forty. They know one shepherd.

profession.toolsmith.1: A badly tempered pickaxe breaks in the worst tunnel.
profession.toolsmith.2: I sharpen better under a waxing moon. Superstition, you'll say. Results, I say.
profession.toolsmith.3: The tools of %2$s are known by the sound of the anvil.
profession.toolsmith.4: Six axes to sharpen and the woodcutter's coming this afternoon.
profession.toolsmith.5: A well-made stone hoe outlasts a badly tempered iron one.
profession.toolsmith.6: The miners of %2$s bring me broken pickaxes the way you'd bring a wounded dog.
profession.toolsmith.7: Small shears are the most work of all. You'd never think it.
profession.toolsmith.8: If you're going down the mine, %1$s, take two pickaxes. You always need the second.
profession.toolsmith.9: The whetstone talks. If it squeals, the edge isn't right.
profession.toolsmith.10: They bring me gold tools to mend. I tell them the truth: they're not worth it.
profession.toolsmith.11: Tempering is knowing when to stop. The rest is brute force.
profession.toolsmith.12: I carve every handle myself. A tool that doesn't sit right in the hand is useless.
profession.toolsmith.13: An anvil wears down, though you'd not think it. Mine has a tired face these days.

profession.weaponsmith.1: A sword doesn't make the warrior, but it helps a lot.
profession.weaponsmith.2: Many adventurers pass through here. Few come back to pay for the sharpening.
profession.weaponsmith.3: Be careful out there, %1$s. Pillagers give no warning.
profession.weaponsmith.4: Four swords on order for the guard, and I'm running out of coal.
profession.weaponsmith.5: An axe cuts trees and heads alike. I don't ask which one you want it for.
profession.weaponsmith.6: They say diamond swords never break. I've seen one snapped in two.
profession.weaponsmith.7: The guard of %2$s complains about how heavy the swords are. Let them complain about scars.
profession.weaponsmith.8: You look after a blade like an animal: water, oil, and never leave it out overnight.
profession.weaponsmith.9: If you face a vindicator, %1$s, don't give him time to raise his axe.
profession.weaponsmith.10: A sword without a scabbard is a dog without a leash: one day it bites the wrong man.
profession.weaponsmith.11: I forge by day and polish by night. The shine on the blade lets me sleep easy.
profession.weaponsmith.12: My grandfather's whetstone is still here. He isn't. That's how it goes.
profession.weaponsmith.13: I don't sell a weapon to anyone who won't look me in the eye when they pay.
